title: Will the rule of law survive the clash of superpowers?
description: DESPITE the risks of war coming from the United States’ current military actions in the Caribbean, some geopolitical analysts seem to believe Russia and China’s presence in Venezuela will serve as a countervailing force and restrain any US impulse to rush into war. It would spare the world a repeat of the Cuban missile crisis of 1962 and allow multilateral forces to create a new geopolitical balance, away from the US-led unipolar world into the new multipolar world led by Brics (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa). It would still be a messy world but hopefully without a new war. This leaves the Chinese-US conflict over Taiwan the more pressing problem in international affairs.
